proposal.utterance: How should 'sustaining practice' (the practice that sustains an institution over time) be classified in BFO?

entities.label: SustainingPractice
entities.rationale: A sustaining practice is a temporally extended happening — repeated performances of acts (e.g., compliance, enforcement, adjudication) by agents — that unfolds over time and thereby keeps an institution in existence. This fits BFO Process (BFO_0000015): it is an occurrent that has temporal parts, involves participants, and is not a static continuant. It is not a disposition or quality because it is something that actually happens rather than a potential or property inhering in a bearer. It is not a generically dependent continuant because it is not an information artifact that can be copied; it is the actual doing. Some might argue for Disposition (BFO_0000016) on the grounds that an institution has a 'tendency' to be sustained, but the practice itself — the aggregate of acts — is a process. A disposition that grounds the practice could be modeled separately as a LegalExistenceCondition (already in the ontology).

relations.rationale: SustainingPractice is a subclass of Process: instances are temporally extended happenings in which agents participate and which bring about or maintain institutional continuity.

Sustaining practices are behavioral manifestations of legal institutional life; they are the enacted, observable side of institutional persistence. BehavioralLegalManifestation (already in the ontology, parent BFO_0000015) is the appropriate proximate parent class, placing SustainingPractice within the existing class hierarchy.
Instances of SustainingPractice have LegalInstitution instances as participants (the institution is what is being sustained), expressed via the BFO relation has participant (RO_0000057).

open_questions: Should SustainingPractice be understood as a single continuous process or as an aggregate/process-aggregate of discrete repeated acts (e.g., an fiat process boundary / process aggregate)? BFO 2020 has process profiles and process aggregates that may be relevant.

Is there a corresponding Disposition that grounds the sustaining practice — i.e., do you want to model the institution's 'capacity to be sustained' as a separate LegalExistenceCondition individual, distinct from the practice itself?

Should SustainingPractice be restricted to legally recognized practices (e.g., official enforcement acts), or does it include informal social practices (e.g., popular compliance with norms)? This affects whether it should be a subclass of BehavioralLegalManifestation or a broader Process subclass.

Is the sustaining practice the same kind of thing as what Hart calls the 'acceptance' of the rule of recognition by officials? If so, should SustainingPractice be linked to existing individuals such as RecognitionOriginThesis or TemporalPersistenceConditionOfRuleOfRecognition?
proposal.rationale_summary: A 'sustaining practice' — the practice that keeps a legal institution in existence over time — is most naturally classified in BFO as a Process (BFO_0000015). It is a temporally extended occurrent constituted by the repeated or ongoing acts of participants (judges, officials, citizens) whose collective performance maintains the institution. It is not a continuant property or disposition (those would capture the institution's potential or capacity to be sustained, not the actual sustaining), and it is not a generically dependent continuant (it is not an information pattern that can be copied but rather an actual happening in the world). The proposed class SustainingPractice is placed as a subclass of the existing working class BehavioralLegalManifestation (itself a subclass of BFO_0000015), which already captures the behavioral, enacted dimension of legal life. A has-participant relation connects instances of SustainingPractice to instances of LegalInstitution. Several open questions remain about the granularity (aggregate vs. continuous process), the relationship to Hartian acceptance, and whether an accompanying Disposition should be modeled separately.
